title: Synergistic drug combinations and machine learning for drug repurposing in chordoma.
summary: Bayesian models trained on prior chordoma-cell screening data ranked compounds for in-vitro testing; AZD2014 inhibited U-CH1 and U-CH2 cells (IC50 0.35 and 0.61 μM), though maximal U-CH2 inhibition was limited. Separately tested drug-pair synergy is not attributed to AI. No animal or clinical efficacy is shown.
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Collaborations Pharmaceuticals (United States); RTI International

evidence.tested: Indexed primary Results report AZD2014 IC50 of 0.35 μM in U-CH1 and 0.61 μM in U-CH2, with limited maximal U-CH2 inhibition. Afatinib/palbociclib were known-inhibitor comparators; drug combinations were a separate study strategy. Replicate details were not independently assessed.
evidence.unknown: Cell-line activity does not establish animal or clinical efficacy. Complete model-validation and replicate methods were not independently reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian machine-learning inhibition models trained on prior chordoma-cell screening data ranked compounds from an NIH NCATS asset set for in-vitro testing; the drug-combination experiments were a separate study strategy.

source_review.scope: Indexed Nature primary abstract and Results passages on Bayesian selection, single-agent activity, and separately tested combinations; complete Methods not independently reviewed.
